full_judgment:
4. Including the investigating officer himself thirteen witnesses in all were examined on behalf of the prosecution. P.W. 8. Juruj Ali. P.W. 10 Sideman and P W. 13 Manik Munshi were tendered by the prosecution for cross-examination but the defence declined to cross-examine P.Ws. 3 and 10. The defence cross-examined P.W. 12. On examination of the trial court record it appears that the learned Additional Session Judge did not record the statement of all the accused appellants except the accused appellants Kedarbap and Badsha after examining them under section 342 Cr.P.C. In the order dated 24.12.70 in the order sheets of the trial court records it appears. that it is recorded there that the accused persons were examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. and their statements were recorded in separate sheets and that on being asked the accused persons pleaded nit gaudy 40040 to adduce: any evidence on defence but the sheet of papers where statements of all the accused appellants except accused appellant Kedarbap and Badsha were to be recorded only contain the questions which were to be proved to those accused appellants. The thumb impression of the accused appellants were taken in those sheets as well as the Additional Sessions Judge hims self also signed in those sheets. But answer given by the accused appellants except accused appellants Kedarbap and Bedeha were not written in those sheets. Mr. Mohammad Ayub, the learned Advocate for the State contends before me that as in the order dated 24-12-70 of the order-sheet of trial court record shows that the accused appellants were examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. and that they pleaded not guilty and declined to adduce evidence. Recording the statements of the accused appellants except Kedarbap and Badsha has not been a fatal defect. It is also contended by him that as the accused appellants Kedarbap and Beduins were examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. and their answer recorded there cannot be any reasons why the other accused appellants would not be examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. Even if it be taken that those accused appellants were examined under section 342 Cr.P.C. non-recording of their statements by the tearteed Additional Sessions Judge cannot but be prejudicial to those accused appellants. Moreover, If the statements of accused Kedar-bap and Badsha after their examinations under section 342 Cr.P.C. there cannot be any surprising reasons why the statements of other accused appellants could not be recorded after examination under section 342 Cr.P.C. In the case of Jalil Bux and another vs. Anu Mian reported in 9 DLR page 73 the Trial court did not record statements of the accused after examination under section 342 Cr.P.C. Akbar. J (as his Lordship then was) observed the judgment delivered by him in that case which runs: 

 I would observe, however, with reference to the other contention for Crown, that it is hazardous preceding for a court, which finds that a fundamental rule of criminal justice, such as that embodied in terms in section 342, Criminal Procedure Code, has been infringed to concern itself with speculations as to what use the accused person would have made of the legal right to an opportunity to explain every piece of evidence weighing against him, had it been allowed to him. His attitude would be based on his own ample knowledge of the circumstances which brought about his arrest and accusation, and determined by his judgment based on or assisted by legal evidence, as to the manner in which he could best serve his own interests, in the exigencies of the trial. It is Impossible for the court either to possess his knowledge or to stimulate his point of view In this regard".
